title: Design a module boundary for a new notifications subsystem
description: The fixture repository needs a new 'notifications' subsystem (email, SMS, and in-app notifications) that several existing modules (orders, billing, auth) will need to trigger. Produce a design proposal (a written document plus a minimal interface/type skeleton, no full implementation) defining the subsystem's public boundary, how existing modules depend on it, and how new notification channels are added without modifying existing callers.
acceptanceCriteria: The proposal defines a single public interface that all three existing modules depend on, with no existing module needing to know which concrete channel(s) are configured.
The proposal explains how a new notification channel is added without modifying any existing caller module.
The proposal explicitly addresses failure handling (e.g. one channel failing should not fail the others) and where that responsibility lives.
A minimal TypeScript interface/type skeleton (no business logic) matches the described public boundary and compiles.
The proposal explicitly states what is out of scope (e.g. delivery-status tracking, retry queues) rather than silently omitting it.
verificationMethod: architecture-check (human-review as primary authority): reviewed against the acceptance criteria above by a human or senior-review process; the interface skeleton is additionally verified to compile.
groundTruth: A correct design centers on a single NotificationDispatcher interface exposing a channel-agnostic send(notification) method, with per-channel adapters implementing a shared NotificationChannel interface registered into the dispatcher, isolating per-channel failures from each other and from callers.
